articles.summary: Como gets some love after that scoreline against Man United midweek
articles.body:
Radio 5 Live , · 22 Oct 2026 , · 49 mins

This week John Bennett is joined by James Horncastle (fresh back from his trip to Como) and Julien Laurens where the focus is all on that remarkable scoreline from Italy after Como beat Manchester United midweek. They show the Italian side some love and hear from Cesc Fabregas. James also sprinkles some Hollywood stardust on to the match after Superman was spotted in the stands – and John and Jules ask that all important question… does James have as much power as Superman? The guys take look at some of the out of work managers on the continent who could be interested if Michael Carrick leaves Manchester United, and Antonio Conte certainly gets a mention. Attention then turns to the injury to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and what impact that will have on PSG’s season. And delve into Serie A and Ligue 1 where it’s tight at the top. John, Jules and James (the three J’s) then look ahead, not only to El Clasico but also the top of the table clash in Dutch football taking place this weekend where Marcel van Der Kraan joins the pod ahead to PSV Eindhoven v Feyenoord. articles.title: North West, 13, Debuts Neck Piercing After Telling People ‘Don’t Judge a Book by Its Cover’
articles.summary: Kim Kardashian and Kanye West‘s daughter, North West, has a piercing in a new place. On Monday, October 19, the 13-year-old posted a TikTok video — set to th...
articles.body:
Kim Kardashian and Kanye West 's daughter, North West , has a piercing in a new place.

On Monday, October 19, the 13-year-old posted a TikTok video — set to the 2004 song "The Reason" by Hoobastank — showing off her edgy look, which included a seemingly faux neck piercing, a blue wig, black grillz, dramatic makeup with a dark-colored lip and long acrylic nails with studs.

As for her outfit, the teenager wore a frilly shirt with a Peter Pan collar and a black skirt.

The faux neck piercing appears to be new for North, who often sports piercings on her face and hand.

As In Touch reported last week, North recently appeared on a TikTok live with Kim, 45, where she insisted she's "not demonic" because of her bold style, telling people, "don't judge a book by its cover," per a clip posted on X .

"Yeah, I feel like people say that because [of] the black grillz and just, like, piercings and stuff," the Skims founder chimed in, to which North said, "Yeah, but I don't know why you guys should [associate] that with demonic cause I don't get that."

Additionally, North, who was wearing a bunch of faux studs on her face during the livestream, explained, "These piercings are not real. I change them so much that you guys think that's real?"

While North said that she wants her cheeks pierced, Kim told her daughter, "We can glue on for now."

North gushed over her love of piercings in an August interview with Dazed , telling the outlet, "They just make you your full self. I really want to get my bridge pierced, but I'm not allowed."

articles.summary: Evento será de 1º a 8 de novembro e terá concurso internacional de cervejas. Novidade é competição inédita dedicada a bebidas sem álcool.
articles.body:
Xanddy Harmonia e Solange Almeida no Bahia Beer Festival — Foto: Redes sociais dos artistas

Capital baiana da cerveja , Alagoinhas vai realizar mais uma edição do Bahia Beer Festival de 1º a 8 de novembro. Neste ano, a programação gratuita contará com shows de Xanddy Harmonia e Solange Almeida, espaço para gastronomia e a tradicional Corrida da Cerveja.

De acordo com a organização, o concurso contará com jurados de 26 países e amostras inscritas por cervejarias de todos os continentes. Essas amostras devem ser enviadas até 25 de outubro. A avaliação será realizada às cegas, entre os dias 2 e 5 de novembro.

O evento receberá ainda a sétima edição do Congresso Internacional da Cerveja (Conib) e vai promover a terceira edição do Brazilian International Beer Awards (BBA), concurso internacional do setor.

O principal destaque desta edição é o BBA Zero, concurso que, segundo os organizadores, será o primeiro do mundo dedicado exclusivamente a cervejas sem álcool. Outra novidade é a participação de uma pessoa surda no júri do BBA — iniciativa anunciada como um avanço na acessibilidade e na diversidade do setor.

O Brazilian International Beer Awards terá a coordenação técnica de Anna Bettu, fundadora da German Beer Academy, instituição alemã dedicada à formação de sommeliers de cerveja.

Entre os jurados confirmados está o alemão Markus Raupach, autor de mais de 60 livros sobre cerveja e integrante de associações de escritores especializados no tema da Grã-Bretanha e da América do Norte.

Segundo Develon da Rocha, CEO da Sol Eventos, empresa organizadora do concurso, a participação de especialistas de diferentes países contribui para elevar o nível das avaliações e fortalecer o reconhecimento internacional do evento.

A cerimônia de premiação do BBA e do BBA Zero está marcada para o dia 5 de novembro, às 19h30.

Bahia Beer 2026: Concurso internacional de cervejas — Foto: Foto: Arquivo Bahia Beer/Secom Alagoinhas

O Congresso Internacional da Cerveja (Conib) será realizado nos dias 4 e 5 de novembro, com a participação de palestrantes e pesquisadores do mercado cervejeiro mundial.

Entre os nomes confirmados está o alemão Matthias Kopp, consultor de cervejarias, sommelier de cerveja certificado pela Doemens Academy, juiz internacional de cervejas e integrante da British Guild of Beer Writers, associação britânica de jornalistas, escritores e comunicadores especializados no setor.

Realizado pelo Governo da Bahia, por meio da Secretaria de Turismo do Estado (Setur-BA), em parceria com a Prefeitura de Alagoinhas, o Bahia Beer Festival busca fortalecer o protagonismo do município no setor cervejeiro. A cidade abriga grandes indústrias do segmento e conta com a reserva estratégica do Aquífero São Sebastião.

articles.title: Kendra Wilkinson Says She’s Fine ‘Looking Old’ If It Means ‘Certain Men’ Leave Her Alone: ‘I Have Nothing for You Guys’
articles.summary: The former reality star says she’s “happy and free” and remains unbothered by the opinions of others
articles.body:
Kendra Wilkinson says critical comments about her appearance do not affect her happiness

Wilkinson shares two children with ex-husband Hank Baskett and often posts about their sports activities

In a Tuesday, Oct. 20 Instagram post, Wilkinson spoke about being okay with losing "certain men" as viewers as she ages

Kendra Wilkinson says she's fine with looking her age — especially if it causes her to lose a certain type of follower.

The Girls Next Door alum, 41, wrote that she's "been in a phase of wanting to lose certain men as viewers even if it takes looking old," on a selfie posted to her Instagram Stories on Tuesday, October 20.

"I have nothing for you guys. Time to go. LOL BUTTT I see the good ones and I appreciate the respect," Wilkinson added.

Wilkinson's post came after she says she received a message from "some dude" suggesting that she "need[s] a makeover" in the comments of a post about her kids' sports.

Wilkinson, who shares two children — son Hank , 16, and daughter Alijah , 12, — with ex Hank Baskett , often shares videos of her kids' sporting events online. "It's so weird the fact people think I owe them that," she said of the remark. "I'm happy and free."

It's not the first time the former Playboy star has drawn a line between her previous, public-facing career and her new, more low-key life.

"Sexy is the last thing I want to be," the former model said in the caption of an August 10 Instagram post. "I aim for health, happiness, success and gods light. Peace is everything to me."

Wilkinson was just 18 when she first moved into the Playboy Mansion. She began starring on the E! reality show The Girls Next Door when she was 19.

"I see people poking at me for my body and my aging and it's ok. I'm at peace and none of that stuff bothers me. I am happy being me and alive and watching my kids grow. If people want to be negative, that's their energy not mine," she said in August. "I'm ok not being Playboy skinny anymore or bleached blonde 21 yr old. That was a time of my life but now I'm older and have lived a life."

Now, Wilkinson believes that her current era is the "greatest phase of my life," as the reality-star-turned-realtor shared in an Oct. 20 Instagram post.

"In the stands watching my kids play their sports, cooking with my son in the mornings, laying on the beach or smoothies with my daughter listening to her heart and all the other little moments," she said. "I'm one lucky mama."

articles.title: Who will be the next James Bond? Amazon MGM reportedly plans final screen tests for these 3 actors
articles.summary: Amazon MGM says casting for the next James Bond is underway, and that major actors are in the running.
articles.body:
The name's Bond — James Bond. That much we know. But who will be the next man behind the famous moniker?

Back in May 2026, Amazon MGM Studios, the company that now has creative control over the Ian Fleming-created franchise, said that the casting process was underway . This week, Deadline reported that final screen tests are scheduled to begin, with actors Callum Turner ( Eternity ), Jack Lowden ( Slow Horses ) and Josh O'Connor ( Challengers ) in the mix. An unknown actor is also expected to test for the part. Jacob Elordi, once a fan favorite for the role, is not screen testing, according to TheWrap .

Amazon MGM has not publicly confirmed the actors who are testing for the role.

The British secret agent has been portrayed by multiple actors since Sean Connery's debut in 1962's Dr. No . Most recently, Daniel Craig starred as Bond across five films, beginning with 2006's Casino Royale and ending with 2021's No Time to Die , which saw the death of his version of 007.

Here's what we know about the future of Bond — including who might portray him next.

In February 2025, Amazon MGM Studios reached a deal with longtime James Bond producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson, giving the company creative control over the 007 franchise for the first time. This came four years after Amazon reached a deal to purchase MGM, in part because of the success of the Bond franchise.

Now, Amazon MGM Studios is making moves to bring a new version of the super spy to life. Director Denis Villeneuve was tapped to helm the next installment of the franchise, with his Dune producer, documentary filmmaker Tanya Lapointe, signing on as an executive producer. Amy Pascal, producer of Project Hail Mary, and David Heyman, producer of all eight Harry Potter films , will produce the movie.

Screenwriter Steven Knight — known for Eastern Promises and the Peaky Blinders TV series — is writing the screenplay, and in September, he confirmed a draft is complete .

"It has always been on my bucket list, and it's fantastic to be invited to do it," Knight said in a 2025 interview with BBC Radio 5 Live Breakfast . "I can't wait to get started. I'm hoping that, being a Bond fan for so many years, it will be imbued into me and I will be able to produce something that's the same but different and better, stronger and bolder."

At CinemaCon in April, Courtenay Valenti, Amazon MGM's head of film, praised the creative team, stating that they were "setting the stage for something that's truly worthy of the Bond legacy."

The casting of Bond has been very hush-hush, with Variety reporting in May that casting director Nina Gold is helping to find the ideal actor to portray the character. Gold is known for casting shows like Game of Thrones and The Crown as well as films like Conclave and Hamnet , the latter of which earned her a nomination for the Academy Awards' first-ever casting Oscar.

While Bond has been played by a relatively unknown actor before (George Lazenby, the Australian actor who portrayed Bond in the 1969 film On Her Majesty's Secret Service , had no film experience before becoming 007), it is likely that a known actor will land the part this time around.

In November 2023, Broccoli told Yahoo Entertainment , "We're totally open to casting a non-star, but acting is a very specialized profession, and if somebody has to carry a movie and have the range of requirements [for Bond] in terms of physicality, it's not going to be someone who has never done it before."

Pascal hinted that fans may know who Bond is by the end of 2026, telling Deadline in August it was a "good bet."

Who has spoken out about the Bond rumors?

The reported final contenders for Bond have not commented publicly about the casting process. Turner told reporters at the Berlin Film Festival earlier this year that it was too early for that conversation and that he would not comment on it. In an August interview with Esquire , he had the same response when asked multiple times about a potential Bond role.

"I don't know anything, so I can't comment," Turner, who recently starred in the romantic comedy One Night Only , said. "There's nothing for me to comment on."

In a 2023 interview with Screen Daily , Lowden commented on rumors about the Bond casting, telling the outlet, "People have said this to me a lot, and it is flattering. I'm not an idiot; if you run about in a suit, it sort of suggests itself. But no, I haven't [screen-tested], I haven't done anything. Slow Horses takes all my time."

However, more recently, rumors have begun to circulate that Lowden is among the final contenders for the role. In August, BBC television presenter Richard Osman also said during an episode of The Rest Is Entertainment podcast that he heard Lowden might be the next Bond .

Lowden's Slow Horses costar Gary Oldman also told Canada's Global in September, "It's been rumored that he's on the shortlist. We're going to find out pretty soon, aren't we? Because they have picked him. They have made their choice, but they have not announced it yet. So my fingers are crossed for Jack."

He later clarified that he was merely expressing support for Lowden and that he did not know if his costar would get the role.

Meanwhile, Lowden's wife, actor Saoirse Ronan, told the Associated Press in October that the subject has not been "coming up in our house, to be honest."

"The dog needs to be walked, the dinner needs to be made — we're most focused on that," she said.

O'Connor, who shared the screen with Craig in 2025's Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery , also skirted the 007 issue in a January 2025 interview with Deadline .

"The truth is that … I think in the space of a week, I made a joke about, wouldn't it be funny if I played Bond? Then, me and Daniel [Craig] did an Actors on Actors , and then something else happened, and then suddenly I was James Bond," he said of the rumors. "If I am Bond, I don't know about it."

For a while, it seemed like any and every charming actor, particularly those who hailed from Britain, were in the mix for the role — and forced to respond to the rumors. Rege Jean-Paul of Bridgerton fame told The Tonight Show in 2021 that speculation around him as the next Bond was "like a merit badge" — but stopped short of confirming any casting rumors.

Idris Elba, a longtime fan favorite for the part, fueled speculation in December 2025 when he posed at a wax museum alongside statues of actors who had previously played the role. But it came nearly three years after Elba shut down those very rumors , telling reporters at the World Government Summit in 2023, "You know, a lot of people talk about another character that begins with 'J' and ends with 'B,' but I'm not going to be that guy. I'm going to be John Luther. That's who I am." And he previously told The Shop podcast in 2022 that playing Bond was not a "goal" of his career.

Aaron Taylor-Johnson, once also rumored to be in the mix, said at the June 2025 premiere of his film 28 Years Later that he can't talk about the casting speculation . He previously told the magazine Numéro that it's "charming and wonderful that people see me in that role" and that he takes it as a great compliment.

Spider-Man star Tom Holland was also rumored to be in the mix. In August 2025, on Gordon Ramsay's YouTube series Scrambled , in August 2025, "I mean, every young British actor, it's the pinnacle of working in our industry." Holland is a big fan of the franchise, even pitching an origin story for the character to a studio in 2022.

Meanwhile, Babygirl star Harris Dickinson, another British actor thought to be in the running, spoke to a reporter about Bond at Cannes in May, teasing that Wicked star Jonathan Bailey would be a great choice . Bailey previously told BBC Radio 2's Breakfast Show in June 2025 that it would be "hard to say no" to the role .

Also in May, Variety reported Tom Francis, a Broadway star known for Sunset Blvd. and Season 4 of Netflix's You , was in the mix.

It's still anyone's guess who will earn the 007 title and take that martini "shaken, not stirred." As with any good Bond movie, we're waiting in suspense.

articles.title: I know Elizabeth Holmes is a fraud. So why was I rooting for her?
articles.summary: A new documentary codirected by Nathan Fielder attempts to understand Elizabeth Holmes as she prepares for her prison sentence.
articles.body:
I know — and we should all know — that Elizabeth Holmes is a fraudster . The former CEO of the failed blood-testing company Theranos was convicted in 2022 on three counts of wire fraud and one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud. For more than a decade, her role in the scam has been rehashed in articles, podcasts, books and a fictionalized TV show.

So why does it seem like so many of us are still hoping to root for her, to unearth some sort of exculpatory evidence that complicates the narrative of her as a villain?

You Can See Everything, a critically lauded new documentary, follows Holmes and her partner Billy Evans as she prepares for her 11-year prison sentence. The subjects' goal, they state on camera, is to grant total access to their home lives to challenge public scrutiny of Holmes. This is a fairly obvious ploy for empathy that almost spoils its own shot: Look at this mom, disheveled and overwhelmed, with her big, watery eyes and perpetual split ends . She's going to prison, even though she swears she's never told a lie.

But the person Holmes and Evans choose to give access to is perhaps the most bizarre and fascinating documentarian possible. The film's co-director, who's shown on camera more than Holmes herself, is comedian Nathan Fielder. His breakout moment came from the show Nathan for You, in which he satirically pulled off dozens of business scams — you know, the kind of thing Holmes is trying to absolve herself from. He moves in with Holmes and her family in the 34 days before she turns herself in.

In one scene, Fielder, who is not an investigative journalist or a scientific expert but also not a pushover, interrogates Holmes about the ineffectiveness of Theranos's now infamous blood-testing device. She maintains that it can do everything she said it could (which, I must emphasize again, is demonstrably and unequivocally false). But it's the same argument she hewed to in court. Her insistence suggests she might actually believe that's the truth. And ultimately, the documentary focuses more on her persona and her relationship with the truth than on the details of the scam that's already been settled in the eyes of the law.

Fielder said at a post-screening Q&A in September that Holmes came across as "so genuine," he wanted to believe her too, even though "I know she's a liar."

But in his unfettered access to Holmes's family, a new narrative does take shape: Evans emerges as the real antagonist . He commands conversations, takes control of Holmes's image and constantly speaks for her, even on X. We start to see Holmes as just a passenger in her own life, overpowered by a man who clearly wants to capitalize on her infamy but won't even let her beat her own eggs.

As Evans talks about wanting to start a mysterious new venture with Holmes, it's hard to ignore how a pattern is emerging — she's going into business with someone she's in a relationship with, who has a much stronger personality than her. At Theranos, Holmes was in a relationship with the company's COO, Sunny Balwani, who was 19 years her senior when they became romantically involved (she was 19 years old at the time). She claims he emotionally and sexually abused her while manipulating her into fraudulent business decisions, which he denies .

In an Oct. 19 essay for Stat News , Theranos whistleblower Tyler Shultz writes, "I've always thought that Elizabeth was with Sunny in part because of his abusive personality, knowing she could use it to her advantage." Shultz believes that Balwani abused Holmes, but that Holmes also set Balwani up to be the company's fall guy. In court, he was convicted on all 12 counts, but she was convicted on only four.

We're left to wonder if Holmes is easily manipulated by these men because she's vulnerable, or whether she chooses coercive partners because she can use them to her advantage. Fielder wonders this too.

Another line of inquiry the documentary explores: whether Holmes, with her highly specific (and meme-able ) affect, may be neurodivergent . Fielder probed his own possible neurodivergence on his previous TV show The Rehearsal . In his interactions with Holmes, it's clear he recognizes something similar in her — for instance, she claims not to understand what's funny about the famous Abbott and Costello " Who's on First?" comedy routine .

It seems that Holmes wants us to think of her as a mom who operates on a different wavelength from the rest of the world. So much of her initial success at Theranos was likewise predicated on the fact that she was a successful young woman in a cutthroat field who was just a little odd. The way she always looks a little uncomfortable and out of place has made her a joke on the internet, and we're not laughing with her.

John Carreyrou, the journalist whose bombshell reporting on Theranos brought the company down in 2015, has a different read. He loves the documentary because of how boldly it puts her lies on display.

"By letting them train their ultra-long zoom lenses on her face while subjecting herself to Mr. Fielder's polite but insistent questioning, Ms. Holmes handed them — and us — a microscope with which to observe and dissect her lies," he writes for the New York Times . The long stares, head nods and half-smiles I saw as heartbreaking indicators that she's out of touch with social cues, Carreyrou saw as tells.

Still, even after parsing all this evidence, I cannot shake my empathetic feelings toward Holmes, and I know I'm not alone, despite the reality of her crimes.

"The woman that I saw on screen looked, frankly, like a broken woman," Shultz, who arguably has more reason to be mad at her than anyone else, says in an interview with CBS . "She is not playing victim. She is an actual victim."

Niloufar Esmaeilpour, a therapist, tells me that it makes sense we're inclined to root for Holmes's redemption. But it also means that she's pulling one over on us just like she did her investors.

"It's easier for humans to believe that she was manipulated by men, rather than accept that women could be ruthless manipulators too, as this belief fits better with more typical gender role expectations," she says. "That you would want to cheer for her shows that your innate empathy functions perfectly; therefore, these same manipulations used by Holmes to fool her investors are being exploited by her to hack into the viewers' psychological programming."

It's human to want someone to be redeemed, especially when they're seen as relatable or their victims are seen as imperfect. Anna Delvey, the "fake heiress" scammer who was convicted of grand larceny, among other financial crimes, has appeared on Dancing With the Stars and walked a runway at NYFW . Gypsy Rose Blanchard , who pleaded guilty to plotting her mom's murder after years of alleged medical abuse, was released from prison to "yasss queen!" fanfare that gave her a career as an influencer. Even Jen Shah, the former Real Housewives of Salt Lake City cast member who was incarcerated with Holmes after pleading guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud , has returned to the internet to a chorus of calls for a second chance .

There's perhaps some recognition that there's a double standard at play here, that men are often rewarded for a certain brazenness that women are punished for. Holmes, Delvey, Blanchard and Shah also have compelling backstories in which they overcame some other villain. My compassion is not an endorsement of bad choices, but a desire to find humanity in even the cartoonishly manipulative.

Loi Medvin , a psychologist, found herself having the same conflicting emotions in response to the documentary as I did. On some level, we are both sympathetic to the argument that Holmes, described as the youngest self-made female billionaire in history at age 30 , had to take desperate measures to get ahead. It's not good, but it's relatable. And that's when Medvin dunked on me.

"There's an interesting contradiction here too," she says. "In wanting to see a woman as misunderstood or taken advantage of, we may inadvertently diminish her own agency and responsibility."

If what I really want from Holmes is to see her stand on her own and be successful apart from manipulative men, I have to believe she is capable of making her own decisions. That includes rectifying the harm that she personally caused investors and hopeful patients. She still hasn't done that . Because of that, I want to defend her more than she wants to accept redemption.

Instead of propping her up in my mind as a misunderstood girlboss, I have to do what Shultz, Fielder and so many others have already done: Accept that she is both vulnerable and responsible. She is guilty, though I want her to be innocent.

articles.title: 'Goldbergs’ star Jeff Garlin says he planned to take his own life amid turbulent final days on sitcom
articles.summary: Jeff Garlin reveals he planned to take his own life after his turbulent exit from "The Goldbergs," detailing the crisis that led him to seek help.

Jeff Garlin reached his breaking point after a tumultuous chapter on "The Goldbergs." The comedian, who exited the hit ABC sitcom in 2021 amid allegations of misconduct on set, opened up about his mental health crisis, his struggles with bipolar disorder and the treatment that helped him rebuild his life. Garlin revealed he had planned to take his own life and even told a loved one the exact time he intended to die during his appearance on SiriusXM's "Where Everybody Knows Your Name." "The last scene I ever filmed was me with Tim Meadows, Dave Koechner, and Troy Gentile, who played my son. And it essentially was a Pizza Hut commercial. No one told me," he said. JULIA LOUIS-DREYFUS REVEALS ‘TONS’ OF FRICTION BEHIND THE SCENES OF ‘SEINFELD’ Garlin said he confronted the production team after learning the scene doubled as a pizza advertisement without his knowledge. When producers explained that the money would help hire another writer, he questioned why the corporation behind the show couldn't cover the expense itself. The actor refused to participate in the promotional scene and instead insisted that producers film his character leaving before the pizza appeared. "I left, and I knew I'd never come back to that set again," he said. But walking away from the set didn't mark the end of Garlin's troubles. Garlin said a producer later visited his home and asked what it would take to convince him to return to the show. Although he had no desire to go back, the comedian demanded a substantial raise and a reduced schedule of just one workday per week. To his surprise, producers agreed. articles.title: Netflix faces turmoil as Greta Gerwig's $280 million 'Narnia' movie looks headed for disaster
articles.summary: Greta Gerwig's Netflix "Narnia: The Magician's Nephew" trailer sparks backlash as fans question the $250 million adaptation's tone and direction.
articles.body: Hollywood just can't help itself. The entertainment industry has been in turmoil recently, thanks to a string of inconsistencies. While there have been notable outliers, films that were both critically and commercially successful, there's a much longer list of movies that have failed. Disney's "The Marvels" was a financial disaster, as was "Madame Web," "The Flash," "Lightyear," the atrocious live-action "Snow White" movie, and of course, 2026's "Supergirl." 'SUPERGIRL' SUFFERS CATASTROPHIC 73% DROP, GETS OBLITERATED AT BOX OFFICE BY PATRIOTIC 'YOUNG WASHINGTON' Massive financial losses. A dramatic decrease in audience trust and consumer interest in many entertainment industry projects. There are varying reasons for each, but most have one thing in common: Hollywood doesn't understand audiences or the material they're making, and they're committed to putting their political beliefs and ideology above competence. Based on the early returns from one of Netflix's biggest and most expensive projects, the once-dominant streaming service is soon to release one of its own. And as with many other Hollywood mistakes, it was easily avoidable. Several years ago, in 2023, news broke that Netflix hired director Greta Gerwig to make at least two films based on the legendary C.S. Lewis book series, "The Chronicles of Narnia." This announcement came after Gerwig's latest film, "Barbie," became a box office phenomenon during and after the "Barbenheimer" weekend. Filming on "Narnia: The Magician's Nephew" started in 2025 and wrapped up in time for the first trailer to hit the internet this October ahead of a 2027 theatrical release. To say that the first trailer has been poorly received would be a dramatic understatement. Several sites have reported that browser extensions showing YouTube "dislikes" found that it's racked up over 65,000 such ratings, though there have been positive reactions too. A quick watch of the preview, and some background on Gerwig and her take on "Narnia" explains why. First, the trailer itself looks, well, awful. Special effects and visuals look like something out of a Marvel movie, overblown, obviously fake, and far too modern for the world that most fans of the book series imagine. To drive home the point that this would be for "modern audiences," the studio and creative team chose Led Zeppelin's "Stairway to Heaven" to play over the visuals. Nothing says: "A story written in the 1950s set at the turn of the century and during the early years of World War II in the late 1930's-early 1940s," like Led Zeppelin. Second, Gerwig's preferred version of the story seems to purposefully remove the underlying meaning of it, of Lewis' work and the religious influence behind it. In an interview published in 2018, for example, Gerwig said that while she goes to church, she's "uncomfortable" with "Jesus is my lord and savior" talk, adding that she finds it "creepy." Lewis, of course, famously converted to Christianity and the Narnia stories contain obvious Christian imagery and symbolism. Including the character of "Aslan," a representation of Jesus Christ. Aslan in this film will be voiced by Meryl Streep, a confusing choice, to say the least. Then the trailer depicted The Eagle and Child, the pub where Lewis and author J.R.R. Tolkien met to discuss writing and their stories, being destroyed by the villain in the film. Some interpreted that as a purposeful nod to the audience that this wouldn't be a faithful retelling of the story. And why would it be, when Gerwig's filmography is littered with one specific ideology: feminism. The message of Gerwig's "Barbie" had as much subtlety as throwing a brick through a window. The real world is an oppressive patriarchy, while the Kens taking over in the Barbie world is an abject disaster that must be fixed by the Barbies returning to rule their fictional world. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Her adaptation of "Little Women" was similarly obvious in its goals, eschewing Jo's marriage from the novel because Gerwig thought it better represented Louisa May Alcott's vision. There's nothing wrong with Gerwig making films that align with her worldview. The issue is that the Narnia story doesn't, and as we've seen over time, forcing ideology into movies where it doesn't belong simply does not work. While she's maintained that she's a devoted, life-long fan of the stories and Lewis himself, the trailer looked like it came from someone who's never thought about them, let alone understood them. Even worse for Netflix? They gave her a reported $250 million budget, at least, to make it. At the time, Gerwig was the hottest filmmaker in the business, thanks to the runaway financial success of "Barbie." But throwing that much money at a director who wants to put a modern ideological spin on every movie she makes? It's insane. And it's clear that Netflix CEO Ted Sarandos has seen the writing on the wall. While there are likely other factors at work beyond just "Narnia" being a potential financial failure, Netflix this week went on a stunning spree of removing top film executives. After a decade there, Sarandos fired Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria. Then Dan Lin, their now-former head of film, and his top lieutenant, Doug Belgrad. Netflix is famously ruthless, but these are not decisions made on the spur of the moment, and it hints at broader problems within their film division. Years of poor quality content and politically motivated projects have taken their toll on subscriber growth. Problems that would only be exacerbated if "Narnia" flops. It's been rumored that the film was subjected to extensive reshoots after dismal test scores at screenings over the summer. Rumors that seem likely to be true, given Netflix pushed the release date back from late 2026 to February 2027. Hardly a time for a blockbuster, $250 million+ movie. Now the first trailer's been greeted with a surge of negative reactions and disappointment. As it always would, given Gerwig's specific penchant for storytelling and inability to remove her own biases. Fittingly, Gerwig discussed the movie with of all people, Stephen Colbert, at a recent exclusive IMAX preview. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD "Narnia" might turn out to be better than expected. Maybe the Streep casting as Aslan won't be the distraction many feared. Maybe Gerwig didn't pour her predictable beliefs into a story that can't accommodate them. Or the off-putting fever dream visuals might be less prevalent than the trailer makes them look. But given the test screenings, her track record and the visuals, it's hard to give her the benefit of the doubt. If audiences don't either, it'll be the latest in a long series of predictable financial failures from Hollywood. And as always, it's their own fault.

articles.title: Spotify says yes, it is busting people for using Family Plan sharing too widely
articles.summary: Spotify CEO Alex Norström confirmed on an earnings call that a new QR code verification method is about closing “holes” on family plan sharing.
articles.body: Spotify co-CEO Alex Norström confirmed on this week’s earnings call that the company is trying to catch Spotify Family plan users who don’t actually live together with a new QR code verification method that requires scanning the plan manager’s phone. TechCrunch reports that in response to a question about the “crackdown,” he called it a “routine improvement” instead: > This is not as much a crackdown as it is actually a routine improvement of our verification methods for our Family Plan. Family Plan has existed for a long while. It has been around for, I think it is now close to 12, 13 years in Spotify history, and it makes up a pretty significant proportion of our subscriber base. > As such, it is important for us to just make sure over time that we improve the verification methods that we have. There are certainly ways, over time, to find holes around it. As that happens, we figure out how to improve it over time. This is not something that has an end date. This is not an implementation that is going to complete. This is just ongoing routine. This isn’t the first time Spotify has tried to limit sharing Family plans, which it says are only for people living in the same household. The new QR code verification method has forced some users to get creative to stay on their shared Premium subscriptions — the code refreshes every few seconds and anyone who misses the seven-day window to scan it gets banned from joining a different Family or Duo plan for 12 months.

articles.title: Raye wins Mercury Prize for 'This Music May Contain Hope'; singer praised for 'scale, structure, ambition and sheer charm'
articles.summary: Singer Raye won the Mercury Prize for her second studio album \"This Music May Contain Hope\" on Thursday, beating the likes of veteran Paul McCartney, rock
articles.body: Singer Raye won the Mercury Prize for her second studio album "This Music May Contain Hope" on Thursday, beating the likes of veteran Paul McCartney, rock band Suede and rapper Dave for the British music award.Judges praised the "scale, structure, ambition and sheer charm" of the 28-year-old chart-topper's 73-minute record, which blends jazz, orchestral pop, funk and other genres."Hope is a very cheesy word ... but hope is just something that we all need," Raye said while accepting the award at the ceremony held in the northern English city of Newcastle."Music is medicine, so I just hope as well that message comes across to anyone who needs it."First handed out to rockers Primal Scream in 1992, the annual £25,000 ($33,495) Mercury Prize shortlists 12 albums released by British and Irish acts in the United Kingdom in the past year. It is considered less mainstream than the BRIT Awards, Britain's pop music honours, and is open to all music genres.This year's contenders included McCartney, who was nominated for his album "The Boys of Dungeon Lane", and past winners Suede and Dave, who were shortlisted for their respective records "Antidepressants" and "The Boy Who Played The Harp".The nominees also included singer Olivia Dean for "The Art of Loving", former Little Mix star Jade for "That's Showbiz Baby!", and producer Nia Archives, who was recognised for "Emotional Junglist".Band Knats, musicians Kojey Radical and Dove Ellis were also in the running for their respective records "A Great Day In Newcastle", "Don't Look Down" and "Blizzard".Florence + the Machine's "Everybody Scream" and "Help (2)", a compilation album by various artists for War Child, completed the list.Rocker Sam Fender won the prize last year for his third album "People Watching".Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'Mentira' de Marcos Valle na ditadura é perpetuada em álbum em que Mariana Matsui revê 'Fotografia' de Tom Jobim | G1
articles.body:
Marcos Valle tem a música 'Mentira', lançada pelo artista em 1973, regravada no primeiro álbum da cantora nipo-brasileira Mariana Matsui — Foto: Divulgação

♬ Em 1973, ao gravar o álbum “Previsão do tempo”, Marcos Valle caiu no suingue do então emergente trio carioca de samba-funk-jazz Azymuth. Pautado pelo clima pesado do Brasil naquela primeira metade dos anos 1970, década marcada pela repressão da ditadura, o repertório autoral do álbum “Previsão do tempo” destacou a música “Mentira”, parceria de Marcos com o irmão Paulo Sérgio Valle calcada no groove do arranjo.

Por ter sido incluída na trilha sonora da novela “Carinhoso”, exibida pela TV Globo naquele ano de 1973, a faixa “Mentira” chegou a ser editada em single – compacto simples, no jargão do mercado fonográfico brasileiro na época – e, 27 anos depois, a gravação foi sampleada pela banda Planet Hemp no registro original da música “Contexto” (Marcelo D2, BNegão, Black Alien, Rafael Crespo e Zé Gonzalez, 2000).

Decorridos 26 anos do sample do Planet Hemp e 53 da gravação original de Marcos Valle, “Mentira” volta a ser perpetuada por Mariana Matsui no primeiro álbum da cantora e compositora nipo-brasileira, programado para ser lançado na próxima quarta-feira, 28 de outubro, em edição da gravadora japonesa Rambling Records, inclusive no formato físico de CD.

Gravada pela artista com participação do próprio Marcos Valle, “Mentira” é uma das nove músicas do álbum “Mariana Matsui”, gravado no estúdio Da Pá Virada, em São Paulo (SP), com produção musical de Thiago Big Rabello (bateria e percussão) e os toques dos instrumentistas Conrado Goys (violão e guitarra), Fábio Sá (baixo) e Salomão Soares (piano, Rhodes e sintetizadores).

No álbum, além de “Mentira”, a cantora também revê “Fotografia” (1959) – uma das obras-primas do cancioneiro de Antonio Carlos Jobim (1927 – 1994), composta por Tom Jobim sem parceiros – e conta com o toque do violoncelista Jaques Morelenbaum em “Lullaby”, acalanto de autoria de Mariana, criado após a artista descobrir que estava grávida do primeiro filho. Detalhe: a faixa “Lullaby” foi gravada em único take, com o piano de Salomão Soares.

Sucesso do cancioneiro japonês desde que foi o tema lançado em janeiro de 1989 na voz de Hibari Misora (1937 – 1989), seis meses antes da morte da cantora, a música “Kawa no nagare no yō ni” (Akira Mitake e Yasushi Akimoto) ganha toque de bossa nova na gravação feita por Mariana Matsui com Lisa Ono, cantora que, assim como Matsui, também construiu a identidade musical entre o Brasil e o Japão.

Capa do álbum 'Mariana Matsui' — Foto: Paulo Mancini

articles.summary: Programação também conta com festas de Halloween e peças teatrais. Veja o que fazer no Distrito Federal entre sexta-feira (23) e domingo (25).
articles.body:
O fim de semana chegou com muitas atrações e opções de lazer no Distrito Federal. Um dos destaques é o UK Music Festival, que acontece nesta sexta-feira (23), no Espaço Temporâneo, na AABB.

O Buraco do Jazz encerra sua edição de 10 anos nesta sexta-feira e sábado (24), uma programação especial, a partir das 18h, no Centro Cultural Três Poderes. E também na sexta-feira, o espetáculo "U2 One Love & Orquestra" chega a Brasília , em única apresentação no Centro de Convenções Ulysses Guimarães.

A programação também conta com o espetáculo "Futuro do Passado", a Festa Joker – A Fenda, e o Sarau Cultural – Abre-te, Sábado!.

Veja o que fazer no Distrito Federal entre sexta-feira (23) e domingo (25):

Buraco do Jazz encerra temporada de 10 anos

Boulevard promove oficina gratuita de pintura com luz negra

Halloween no Brasília Shopping: uma tarde de doces travessuras

Sarau Cultural – Abre-te, Sábado! em Sobradinho

'Danúbio Azul' é atração gratuita deste fim de semana em Taguatinga

2ª edição da festa 'Deu Match' no Galpão 17

Ordinário Bar & Música tem feijoada, samba e pagode

Nesta sexta-feira (23), o UK Brasil apresenta o UK Music Festival, fora de casa, enquanto a reforma do pub está em andamento. A programação do evento foi pensada para celebrar a trajetória do rock e pop/rock nacional e internacional, com mais de oito horas de festa no Espaço Temporâneo, na AABB.

A noite começa com a discotecagem do DJ Cláudio Lopes, seguida pelas apresentações das bandas Morning Glory, Paulo Mesquita, Zero10, Sereníssima e a banda Válvula.

📍 Local: Temporâneo — AABB (Setor de Clubes Esportivos Sul - SCES)

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$ 67, pelo site

Festival Buraco do Jazz — Foto: Foto: Divulgação

Dez anos de música, encontros e ocupação cultural dos espaços públicos de Brasília merecem ser comemorados juntos, com uma despedida à altura. Por isso, nesta sexta-feira (23) e sábado (24), o Buraco do Jazz promove uma programação especial, a partir das 18h, no Centro Cultural Três Poderes.

Na sexta-feira, Maíra Guedes assume o palco para mais uma noite de música ao ar livre. O gran finale fica para sábado, quando uma banda surpresa abre a programação às 17h, preparando o terreno para o Encontro Racional, às 20h, no último show desta temporada comemorativa.

Além dos shows, o público também pode conferir os produtos da Feira de Artesanato e aproveitar as opções gastronômicas da praça de food trucks.

🗓️ Quando: sexta-feira (23) e sábado (24)

📍 Local: Centro Cultural Três Poderes - Praça dos Três Poderes, Eixo Monumental - no gramado da Bandeira Nacional

🎫 Entrada gratuita (contribuição voluntária)

Banda U2 One Love — Foto: Marcelo Crelece

Considerado o maior tributo ao U2 da América Latina e um dos maiores do mundo, o espetáculo U2 One Love & Orquestra chega a Brasília, nesta sexta-feira (23), em única apresentação no Centro de Convenções Ulysses Guimarães. O espetáculo traz ao público um gostinho da experiência de estar em um show do U2, com performance de palco, instrumentos musicais, aparência, figurinos e sonoridade.

📍 Local: Centro de Convenções Ulysses Guimarães

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$ 88, pelo site

Agrupação Teatral Amacaca em Futuro do Passado — Foto: Diego Bresani

Neste fim de semana, o espetáculo "Futuro do Passado" ocupa o Museu Nacional. A peça conduz o público por diversos espaços do Museu Nacional da República, em uma experiência cênica que une teatro, dança, música e artes visuais. A proposta é voltar para 1922 com o olhar de 2026.

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$ 20, pelo site

A festa Joker – A Fenda acontece neste sábado (24), no Estádio Nacional de Brasília. A festa começa às 21h e promete uma experiência imersiva que mistura música, cenografia temática e atrações em uma ambientação inspirada no universo do caos e da loucura.

Com proposta de transportar o público para uma realidade fora do comum, o evento aposta em experiências e elementos visuais para criar uma atmosfera de Halloween. A organização convida os participantes a entrarem no clima da festa com fantasias e a explorarem a temática da fenda, que dá nome ao festival.

🎫 Ingressos: a partir de R$ 70, pelo site

Cores que brilham no escuro, contrastes intensos e arte fora dos padrões convencionais marcam a oficina Pintura no Escuro, que acontece nesta sexta-feira (23) e sábado (24), no Boulevard Shopping Brasília. A iniciativa para adultos propõe uma imersão no universo das artes visuais, em que a luz negra transforma o ambiente e destaca os efeitos das tintas fluorescentes, ampliando as possibilidades de criação.

A atividade começa com esboços a carvão, seguidos pela aplicação de tintas convencionais e neon. Sob a iluminação especial, as cores ganham novos efeitos visuais, enquanto os participantes exploram combinações, formas e contrastes. Cada pessoa receberá uma tela de 20 x 30 cm e os materiais necessários, além de acompanhamento durante todas as etapas. Ao final, poderá levar para casa a obra produzida.

⏰ Horário: sexta, das 18h às 21h e sábado, das 16h às 19h

📍 Local: Boulevard Shopping Brasília - Espaço Entreartes, piso 2, ao lado da Claro

À medida que outubro avança, uma névoa de encanto e mistério se espalha pelos corredores do Brasília Shopping, transformando o cotidiano em um verdadeiro caldeirão de imaginação. Neste sábado (24), o mall abre as portas para o seu tradicional evento de Halloween, convidando pequenos bruxos, monstrinhos e fadas a celebrarem uma das datas mais lúdicas do ano.

A jornada tem início às 12h com a oficina de pintura de rosto, onde pinceladas coloridas dão vida a criaturas fantásticas e preparam os pequenos aventureiros para o espetáculo. Mais tarde, às 14h, os corredores se convertem em um palco vibrante com a Parada do Terror, que conduz o público em um verdadeiro desfile performático — o momento perfeito para exibir a fantasia escolhida.

Logo em seguida, às 15h, os pequenos partem para a tão aguardada Caça aos Doces: é hora de desvendar enigmas, percorrer os cantos do shopping em busca de “gostosuras ou travessuras” e se divertir a cada pista revelada.

📍 Local: Praça central do Brasília Shopping

🎫 Entrada gratuita, com vagas limitadas (pelo app do shopping) para a Caça aos Doces

Neste sábado (24), Sobradinho recebe mais uma edição do Sarau Cultural – Abre-te, Sábado!, com uma programação gratuita dedicada à música, à poesia, à literatura e às artes. A programação conta com DJ Sista L, Banda Praga de Baiano e Banda Pra Quem Tá Quente, levando ao público diferentes ritmos e sonoridades.

Um dos destaques do evento é o palco aberto, que terá participações especiais de músicos de Sobradinho. As apresentações serão acompanhadas por uma banda formada por Manga (bateria), Pierre Simões (teclado), Junior Morgado (violão) e Zambinha (baixo), incentivando a participação de artistas locais e a diversidade musical.

A poesia e a literatura também estarão presentes, com poetas e escritores compartilhando suas produções com o público. A proposta é aproximar diferentes linguagens artísticas e ampliar os espaços de expressão para os talentos da região.

📍 Local: Estacionamento da Quadra 10/11 – Sobradinho I/DF

Nesta sexta-feira (23) e sábado (24), o Teatro Paulo Autran, no Sesc Taguatinga, recebe o espetáculo "Danúbio Azul". A produção integra o projeto Taguá em Cena 3 e tem apresentações gratuitas abertas ao público sempre às 20h, com retirada de ingressos diretamente no local.

O espetáculo transforma o palco em um grande baile noturno, onde a beleza e a violência, o humor e o estranhamento, o clássico e o grotesco dançam lado a lado. Entre a beleza clássica da valsa Danúbio Azul, composta pelo austríaco Johann Strauss II, e a elegância decadente de uma quadrilha mascarada, o espetáculo mergulha em um universo noturno, fabuloso e inquietante. Dândis, criminosos, amantes e figuras misteriosas atravessam o salão em busca do crime perfeito, ou talvez apenas de uma saída.

📍 Local: Teatro Paulo Autran (Sesc Taguatinga Norte)

🎫 Entrada gratuita, com retirada de ingressos no local

A festa "Deu Match" está de volta ao Galpão 17 nesta sexta-feira (23). A programação musical da noite traz um repertório pensado para não deixar ninguém parado, misturando clássicos e grandes sucessos que marcaram época. Subirão ao palco do Galpão 17 os projetos Go Back 80 e Áudio Hitz, além da discotecagem do DJ Wendel Sousa, garantindo uma noite repleta de rock, hits icônicos e muita energia positiva.

📍 Local: Galpão 17 - SMAS Área Especial G Conjunto A Lotes 16 e 17, Brasília - DF

Neste domingo (25), o Ordinário Bar & Música, no Setor Bancário Sul, promove a Feijuca no Ordi, a partir das 12h, com feijoada à vontade por R$ 59,95, opção vegana e happy hour até as 20h.

A partir das 16h, a programação ganha ritmo com a SECA, que reúne samba, encontros e cerveja. A atração fica por conta do grupo Doze por Oito, com samba e pagode. A entrada é gratuita até as 18h, e a casa abre às 12h.

📍 Local: Ordinário Bar & Música - SBS Q. 2 BL Q Lojas 5/6 - Asa Sul, Brasília - DF

Halloween no JK Shopping — Foto: Divulgação

O JK Shopping preparou uma tarde assustadoramente divertida para celebrar o Halloween com a criançada. Neste domingo (25), o Bailinho de Halloween reúne teatro, personagens, brincadeiras e gostosuras em uma programação gratuita para toda a família.

A diversão começa com o espetáculo A Noiva Cadáver, da companhia Néia e Nando, seguido de animação com a Happy Dreams. Também haverá distribuição de pipoca, algodão-doce, balões e doces, além de pintura de rosto para completar a fantasia dos pequenos.

📍 Local: JK Espaço Arte – Teatro e Galeria (Piso SS) | JK Shopping

articles.title: 'Jailer 2' box office collection day 8: Rajinikanth’s film earns Rs 606.05 cr worldwide; India Net collection reaches Rs 334.35 cr
articles.summary: Rajinikanth’s 'Jailer 2' has recorded Rs 606.05 cr in worldwide gross collections after eight days in theaters.
articles.body: Rajinikanth’s 'Jailer 2' has recorded Rs 606.05 cr in worldwide gross collections after eight days in theaters. According to Sacnilk, the film earned Rs 17.15 cr in India net collections on Thursday, October 22. The latest earnings came from 13,241 shows across multiple language versions. Domestic gross collections have reached Rs 391.55 cr, while overseas markets have contributed Rs 214.50 cr.Thursday’s India net collection declined by 39.1% compared with Wednesday’s Rs 28.15 cr. The film’s extended opening-week total has reached Rs 334.35 cr in India net earnings. Tamil screenings remained the biggest contributor to the latest day’s domestic collections, ahead of Telugu, Hindi and Kannada versions.The Tamil version collected Rs 10.75 cr from 5,883 shows on Thursday. Telugu screenings added Rs 3.60 cr across 2,085 shows, while the Hindi version earned Rs 2.40 cr from 5,095 shows. Kannada contributed Rs 40 lakhs through 178 shows.Tamil accounted for approximately 62.7% of the day’s India net collection. The film recorded 1,189,753 footfalls on Thursday, taking its cumulative footfalls to 22,052,867. Tamil 2D screenings registered 32.75% overall occupancy, with morning shows at 22%, afternoon shows at 30.15%, evening shows at 38.15% and night shows at 40.69%.Telugu, Hindi and Kannada occupancyThe Telugu version recorded 30.68% overall occupancy on Day 8. Morning shows registered 20.33%, followed by 31.17% in the afternoon, 34.17% in the evening and 36.25% at night. Hindi screenings recorded 19.94% overall occupancy. Morning shows registered 10.58%, while afternoon occupancy reached 18.92%. Evening shows recorded 25.92%, followed by 24.33% at night. Kannada screenings reported 38% occupancy, the highest among the four language versions, despite contributing the smallest net collection. articles.title: Julia Roberts honors “Steel Magnolias” dad Tom Skerritt upon his death at 93
articles.summary: Skerritt died of natural causes, his family said in a statement.
articles.body:
Julia Roberts was one of Tom Skerritt's costars who paid tribute to him after his death.

Skerritt and Roberts played father and daughter in the drama costarring Sally Field.

The Top Gun actor's family confirmed the news to Entertainment Weekly .

Julia Roberts remembered her Steel Magnolias costar Tom Skerritt in the hours after his death on Thursday .

Skerritt, 93, played Roberts' dad, Drum, in one of her early but memorable roles, that of Shelby Eatenton Latcherie, in the 1989 movie.

It was a long time ago, but Roberts still had good memories: "A shining light of a gentle man. RIP" she captioned a photo of herself and Skerritt in a scene from the film.

The film about a close-knit group of women living in small-town Louisiana also costarred Sally Field (as Shelby's mom, M'Lynn), and Dolly Parton (Truvy), Olympia Dukakis (Clairee), Shirley MacLaine (Ouiser), and Daryl Hannah (Annelle).

The sweet scene Roberts shared depicts the characters in one of the tearjerker's happier moments: a holiday party in which Skerritt's Drum has recently learned that his daughter is expecting a baby.

After he gets everyone's attention, she says, "Daddy," as a reminder to keep the news quiet.

"Don't worry, honey," Skerritt's character says. "I'm not going to tell them you're pregnant..."

After cheers from onlookers, he adds, "I'm just gonna tell them that I'm gonna be a granddaddy!"

The news causes M'Lynn to worry. While Shelby wants to be a mother, doctors have advised her not to have a child because she's has diabetes. But in the moment, both Skerritt and Roberts' characters are filled with joy.

While Steel Magnolias revolves mostly around the women, Skerritt's character is memorable, not only for the party scene but for earlier moments in which he shoots into his yard in order to scare away the birds ahead of Shelby's wedding to Dylan McDermott's character, Jackson.

MacLaine's Ouiser alleges that the noise is stressing out her dog.

Since news of Skerritt's death broke Wednesday, other former costars have paid tribute to the actor who was also known for his work in movies including Top Gun , MASH , A River Runs Through It , and Contact , as well as '90s TV series Picket Fences .

Lauren Holly, who costarred with Skerritt on the CBS series, which aired from 1992 to 1996, wrote that she " adored Tom Skerritt. "

"I was lucky enough to work with him on more than one project, but the first was Picket Fences ," the actress recalled . "He was our leader. His example made those years such a joy and we all loved and respected him so much. He cared deeply for his family — both the one at home and the one at work. He cared deeply for his planet, and all of its inhabitants. He had a huge impact on my life, and so many memories I have of him include sharing fits of crippling laughter. Rest easy my friend. I will think of you often."

Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter .

Skerritt won an Emmy in 1993 for playing the show's Sheriff Jimmy Brock.

Actress Kathy Baker, who portrayed his spouse on the David E. Kelley series, called him her "dear friend."

"He taught me so much during our four years on Picket Fences ," she said in a statement to Entertainment Weekly 's sister publication PEOPLE . "I couldn't have asked for a more gracious and kind actor to work with, and it was very special to share with him the incredible run of the show."

articles.body:
The Women's First Team are back in Serie A Women action, this time with a Matchday 4 clash against Roma at home.

Let's get up to speed ahead of Saturday's game with some pre-match stats.

Juventus have 21 wins to Roma's eight. Four draws complete the picture, including two in a final that ultimately awarded a trophy each.

Juventus have scored 68 goals against Roma in all competitions, at least three more than against any other opponent in their history.

Juventus leads the way in this season's opening season for both pass completion percentage (87.6%) and average ball possession (67.4%).

Remina Chiba, along with Agnese Bonfantini, is one of two players who have scored more than one goal from the bench in the first three matchdays of this season's Serie A: two each.

Annamaria Serturini played 156 games and scored 41 goals in all competitions for Roma between 2018 and 2024. The 1998-born player has already found the net against her former team in Serie A, scoring for Inter in January 2025.

Gianpiero Piovani has faced Juventus 22 times as a coach in Serie A, with Brescia, Sassuolo, and Inter; the current Roma coach has recorded five wins, four draws, and 13 defeats, and is unbeaten in his four most recent matches (3W, 1D).

Roma, along with Inter and Como 1907, are one of three teams with a perfect record in the newly opened championship and could achieve four wins in their first four Serie A games of the season for the third time in their history - the previous two came in the 2023/24 and 2025/26 seasons.

With one appearance, Manuela Giugliano will become the first player to reach the milestone of 150 Serie A appearances for Roma (149 currently).

articles.title: Headliners revealed for Isle of Wight Festival 2027
articles.summary: The 2027 festival will mark the 25th anniversary of the revival of the legendary rock event in 2002.
articles.body:
Fatboy Slim, Robbie Williams and Kings of Leon have been announced as headliners for next year's Isle of Wight Festival.

The festival, due to take place from 17-20 June 2027 at Seaclose Park in Newport, will be celebrating the 25th anniversary of its revival.

Festival director Caroline Giddings said next year's line up had a "real mix of artists".

The future of the event was secured until 2033 when its licence was renewed in October .

Performances at the 2027 festival will be broadcast on Sky.

Fatboy Slim - real name Norman Cook - has won two Brit Awards and an Ivor Novello Award for Outstanding Contribution to British Music.

Saturday headliner Robbie Williams boasts 90 million album sales worldwide and six of the top 100 best-selling albums in British history.

Multi-Grammy and Brit Award-winning Kings of Leon will close the festival on the Sunday.

Festival director Caroline Giddings said: "Fatboy Slim, Robbie Williams and Kings of Leon each bring something different to the weekend.

"With Becky Hill, Bastille and Myles Smith also on the bill, there's a real mix of artists for different generations and tastes, and there's still more to come.

"We put a lot of thought into what happens beyond the main stages, too.

"The food, the entertainment and the spaces where people can spend time together are all part of what makes it a special weekend on the island."

Also joining the line up are Courteeners, Kaiser Chiefs, Rudimental, 5 Seconds of Summer, Inhaler, Jack Savoretti, Keo, T'Pau, Scouting For Girls and The Cardigans.

Tickets go on general sale at 08:00 on Monday.

The original Isle of Wight Festival began in 1968 and attracted hundreds of thousands of music fans to see artists including Bob Dylan, Jimi Hendrix and The Who.

It was abandoned after crowd chaos at the infamous 1970 event at Afton Down that drew an estimated 600,000-strong audience, more than five times the island's population.

The festival was resurrected in 2002 by promoter John Giddings and has seen artists such as David Bowie, the Rolling Stones and Bruce Springsteen cross the Solent at the Seaclose Park site.

An Isle of Wight Council report said the festival has had a "major economic benefit to the Island", estimated to be worth over £15m a year to the island economy

articles.title: Independent music lets me call the shots: Sravana Bhargavi
articles.summary: A career in playback singing can bring recognition through songs written and composed by others, but carving out a musical identity of one’s own is a
articles.body: A career in playback singing can bring recognition through songs written and composed by others, but carving out a musical identity of one’s own is a different journey. For Telugu singer Sravana Bhargavi, hits such as Simhamanti Chinnode and Super Machi mark one chapter, while independent music has opened up a more personal, unfiltered creative space. Following her recent performance in the city on Sunday, where she brought together both sides of her musical journey, she speaks to Hyderabad Times about stumbling into playback singing, finding her voice through independent music and taking charge of every aspect of her work.‘I never imagined I would sing for films’Music was never part of Bhargavi’s career plan. An engineering student who had learnt Carnatic vocal music since Class VII, she entered the industry after her mother encouraged her to audition for the reality show Sapta Swaralu, where she emerged as the first runner-up. Her playback debut came with Kadantana from Boni, composed by Ramana Gogula, but recording for established composers initially left her questioning herself. “Mani Sharma, Keeravani sir, all these people… I used to think, ‘Oh my God, why is he calling me? Why do these people think that I am fit for this role?’ I think it is called imposter syndrome. I had that,” she recalls.Her first major breakthrough came with Simhamanti Chinnode from Simha, composed by the late Chakri. “I think I sang about 10 songs before that. But that song was my first hit. Everybody started talking about it. That was my visiting card at that point.”My independent journey brought out my authentic self. I’m unapologetic. Take it or leave it, How I conceive an idea and translate it into music is in my control‘I’m unapologetic about who I am’If playback singing introduced Bhargavi to a world she had never anticipated, independent music has given her greater creative ownership. From conceiving an idea to deciding how it sounds and translates on screen, she has a say in the entire process. Her independent catalogue includes Fukuyama and Devara (The Thirst Trap), while Atagani Aata gave her an opportunity to work with lyrics by Goreti Venkanna.“Whatever ideas or songs have come out in my independent sector, everything started as a thought in my head. My independent journey brought out my authentic self. I’m unapologetic. I am this. Take it or leave it. That’s it,” she says. “My sound, how I express myself, conceive an idea and translate it into a music video or into the track — all that is in my control. It’s a very nice feeling by the end of it.”‘Playback singing pampered me a lot’Creative independence, however, comes with the responsibility of managing an entire project. “Playback has pampered me a lot, in a way. There’s a music director who will take care. There’s someone doing the composing. There’s a lyricist. Everything is taken care of. But right now, I’m everything. Right from the top-end things to the puny-level things, everything I’m supposed to take care of,” Bhargavi says. That shift has not meant turning away from playback. “I can’t ignore my movie songs just because I’m doing indie, or I can’t ignore indie for commercial songs. So I will be doing both,” she says, signing off.- Sanjana PulugurthaGet the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.summary: La entrevista de Pedro Sánchez con David Broncano en 'La Revuelta' alcanza 4.387.000 espectadores y un 33,9% de cuota de pantalla
articles.body: La visita de Pedro Sánchez a 'La Revuelta' ha conseguido un resultado histórico en televisión. La entrevista del presidente del Gobierno con David Broncano, emitida este jueves 22 de octubre en La 1, reunió a una media de 4.387.000 espectadores y alcanzó un 33,9% de cuota de pantalla. La cifra supone un récord para el programa de entretenimiento de RTVE y convierte la emisión en una de las grandes citas televisivas del año. La expectación generada por la presencia del jefe del Ejecutivo, en plena precampaña de las elecciones generales del próximo 29 de noviembre, ha impulsado al formato muy por encima de sus resultados habituales. El dato adquiere especial relevancia si se compara con las cifras que venía registrando el espacio presentado por Broncano. Según los registros de FormulaTV, 'La Revuelta' había alcanzado hasta ahora un máximo de 2.706.000 espectadores y un 20,4% de cuota de pantalla, con la visita de Rosalía el 10 de noviembre de 2025. La entrevista a Sánchez supera ampliamente ese registro. La participación del presidente del Gobierno era una de las más esperadas de la temporada. El programa había invitado a los principales candidatos a las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre para entrevistarlos en un formato alejado de los debates políticos tradicionales. Sánchez fue el primero en aceptar la propuesta y sentarse en el sofá de Broncano. Durante la conversación, ambos abordaron cuestiones políticas y personales, con el tono distendido característico del programa. Uno de los momentos más comentados llegó cuando el presentador preguntó al presidente por las críticas que apuntan a que fue él quien impulsó la llegada de 'La Revuelta' a la televisión pública. Sánchez respondió con ironía y defendió el papel del entretenimiento en RTVE, mientras que Broncano aprovechó la ocasión para bromear sobre la relación entre el programa y el Gobierno. La entrevista también incluyó preguntas sobre la gestión del Ejecutivo, la vivienda y otros asuntos de actualidad. La emisión se produjo, además, en un contexto de creciente presencia de los candidatos políticos en los programas de entretenimiento. La estrategia busca llegar a públicos que no necesariamente siguen las entrevistas políticas convencionales y acercar a los aspirantes a la presidencia a través de conversaciones más informales. Los 4,4 millones de espectadores y el 33,9% de cuota representan un salto extraordinario respecto a los datos habituales de 'La Revuelta'. En las semanas anteriores, el programa había registrado cifras sensiblemente inferiores, con entregas que se movían en torno al millón o millón y medio de espectadores, según la jornada y el invitado. El resultado también refuerza el interés televisivo de las entrevistas políticas en un periodo previo a las elecciones. La presencia de Sánchez no solo tenía relevancia por su condición de presidente del Gobierno, sino también por el debate que rodea desde hace tiempo a la relación entre el Ejecutivo y el programa de RTVE.

articles.title: Singer Raye wins Mercury Prize for ‘This Music May Contain Hope’
articles.summary: British Singer Raye won the Mercury Prize for her second studio album “This Music May Contain Hope,” beating the likes ​of veteran Paul McCartney, rock band Suede and rapper ‌Dave for the British music award.
articles.body: LONDON — British Singer Raye won the Mercury Prize for her second studio album “This Music May Contain Hope” on Thursday, beating the likes ​of veteran Paul McCartney, rock band Suede and rapper ‌Dave for the British music award. Judges praised the “scale, structure, ambition and sheer charm” of the 28-year-old chart-topper’s 73-minute record, which blends jazz, orchestral pop, funk and ​other genres. “Hope is a very cheesy word ... but hope is ​just something that we all need,” Raye said while ⁠accepting the award at the ceremony held in the northern English ​city of Newcastle. “Music is medicine, so I just hope as well ​that message comes across to anyone who needs it.” First handed out to rockers Primal Scream in 1992, the annual £25,000 ($33,495) Mercury Prize shortlists 12 albums released by British ​and Irish acts in the United Kingdom in the past ​year. It is considered less mainstream than the BRIT Awards, Britain’s pop music honours, ‌and ⁠is open to all music genres. This year’s contenders included McCartney, who was nominated for his album “The Boys of Dungeon Lane”, and past winners Suede and Dave, who were shortlisted for their respective records “Antidepressants” and “The ​Boy Who Played ​The Harp”. The ⁠nominees also included singer Olivia Dean for “The Art of Loving”, former Little Mix star Jade for “That’s Showbiz ​Baby!”, and producer Nia Archives, who was recognised for “Emotional ​Junglist.” Band ⁠Knats, musicians Kojey Radical and Dove Ellis were also in the running for their respective records “A Great Day In Newcastle,” “Don’t Look Down” and “Blizzard.” Florence + the ⁠Machine’s “Everybody ​Scream” and “Help (2),” a compilation album by various ​artists for War Child, completed the list. Rocker Sam Fender won the prize last year ​for his third album “People Watching.”

articles.title: Jordi Évole reacciona a las audiencias de Pedro Sánchez en 'La Revuelta' y lanza un aviso sobre las elecciones del 29-N: "Las encuestas no lo detectan"
articles.standfirst: Jordi Évole analiza el récord de audiencia de Pedro Sánchez en 'La Revuelta', con 4,3 millones de espectadores, y advierte sobre el interés por las elecciones generales del 29-N.
articles.summary: Jordi Évole analiza el récord de audiencia de Pedro Sánchez en 'La Revuelta', con 4,3 millones de espectadores, y advierte sobre el interés por las elecciones generales del 29-N.
articles.body: La entrevista de Pedro Sánchez en 'La Revuelta' continúa generando reacciones tras conseguir un resultado histórico de audiencia. Una de las más destacadas ha sido la de Jordi Évole, que ha aprovechado los datos de la emisión para lanzar una reflexión sobre el panorama político y las próximas elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre. El periodista ha publicado un mensaje en su cuenta de X en el que interpreta el seguimiento de la entrevista como una posible señal de un movimiento político que todavía no se estaría reflejando en las encuestas. "Algo se mueve que las encuestas, de momento, no detectan. Este dato no es normal. La aldea gala empieza a coger forma", ha escrito. Évole también ha puesto el foco en el interés que, a su juicio, está despertando la campaña electoral y ha advertido a los candidatos que eviten exponerse en entrevistas y debates. "El interés por las elecciones del 29N se dispara. Quién se esconda de entrevistas y debates lo puede pasar muy mal", ha añadido. Aunque el periodista no menciona expresamente a ningún candidato en su publicación, su reflexión llega después de que Alberto Núñez Feijóo y Santiago Abascal no hubieran confirmado su participación en 'La Revuelta', pese a las invitaciones del programa a los principales aspirantes a la presidencia del Gobierno. La reacción de Évole se produce después de que la entrevista de David Broncano al presidente del Gobierno, emitida este jueves 22 de octubre en La 1, alcanzara cifras extraordinarias. El programa registró una media de 4.387.000 espectadores y un 33,9% de cuota de pantalla, según los datos de audiencia difundidos por Barlovento Comunicación a partir de las mediciones de Fifty5Blue. Además, 7.129.000 espectadores conectaron en algún momento con la emisión. La cifra convirtió la entrevista en la emisión de entretenimiento más vista del año y en el programa más visto de la historia de 'La Revuelta', que superó así su anterior récord, conseguido con la visita de Rosalía en noviembre de 2025. Durante su entrevista con David Broncano, Pedro Sánchez abordó algunos de los principales asuntos de la actualidad política. El presidente del Gobierno reconoció que los casos de corrupción vinculados a su partido han sido el peor error de la legislatura y una doble decepción personal. También defendió su política de vivienda, con especial atención al acceso a precios asequibles, y admitió que la gestión de la crisis migratoria de Ceuta podría haberse hecho mejor, aunque reivindicó la cooperación con Marruecos y las medidas adoptadas en las fronteras. El jefe del Ejecutivo también defendió la necesidad de regular las redes sociales para proteger a los menores y controlar los contenidos generados mediante inteligencia artificial. En el plano político, criticó los pactos entre PP y Vox en materia cultural, elogió a Yolanda Díaz y explicó por qué no veía viable la propuesta de Gabriel Rufián para unir a las fuerzas progresistas. Además, habló de sus relaciones con Donald Trump, cuestionó el coste de elevar el gasto en defensa al 5% del PIB y se refirió a las dificultades para reformar la Ley Mordaza. En clave electoral, Sánchez aseguró que confía en ganar las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre con una mayoría más amplia y pidió a los votantes que le faciliten la gobernabilidad. También anunció que está dispuesto a acudir a 'El Hormiguero' y a otros espacios durante la campaña. La conversación dejó espacio, además, para las preguntas personales de Broncano, a las que el presidente respondió con humor, incluida la relativa a su vida sexual.
